lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 4: Your first Pod
lesson.description: Write a Pod manifest, apply it to a kind cluster, then inspect it with get, describe, logs, exec and port-forward, read its phase and delete it.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: A Pod is the smallest thing Kubernetes runs: one IP around one or more containers. Learn get, describe, logs and exec on it, and treat it as disposable.

boards.title: The manifest
boards.hint: four fields you write, and one the cluster writes

rows.name: apiVersion
rows.role: Which version of the Kubernetes API this object uses. Pods are in the core group, version `v1`.

rows.name: metadata
rows.role: Who the object is. At least a `name`. The lesson also sets a namespace and a label.

rows.name: spec
rows.role: The desired state. For a Pod, mainly the list of containers.

rows.name: status
rows.role: What is true right now: the phase, the Pod IP, the conditions. You never put `status` in your file.

boards.note: One network identity: the IP belongs to the Pod, and containers in that Pod talk on `localhost`. One hostname: containers see the Pod name. One place: all containers of a Pod run on the same node. Pods are disposable. Kubernetes never moves a Pod. It replaces it with a new one that has a new UID.

boards.title: Phase, container state, STATUS
boards.hint: three different stories, from the Pod lifecycle docs as the lesson states them

rows.name: Pending
rows.role: Accepted, but at least one container is not running yet. Waiting for a node and pulling images both count.

rows.name: Running
rows.role: Bound to a node, all containers created, at least one running or restarting.

rows.name: Succeeded
rows.role: All containers exited with success and will not restart.

rows.name: Failed
rows.role: All containers have terminated and at least one failed.
rows.where: A phase, not the STATUS word `Error`.

rows.name: Unknown
rows.role: The control plane cannot get the state, usually because the node is unreachable.

rows.name: Container state
rows.role: `Waiting`, `Running` or `Terminated`. A waiting container has a reason, such as `ContainerCreating` or `ImagePullBackOff`. A terminated one has an exit code.

rows.name: restartPolicy
rows.role: `Always` (the default), `OnFailure`, or `Never`. The kubelet waits 10 seconds, then 20, then 40, doubling up to 5 minutes, and resets that timer after 10 minutes without trouble.

steps.title: Life of Pod hello
steps.hint: the events on the lesson's describe, top to bottom

items.what: `Scheduled`. Successfully assigned `k8s-from-zero/hello` to the node. The lesson's node is `k8s-ep04-control-plane`.
`Pulled`. On the lab the image was already present. On your machine you see `Pulling`, then `Successfully pulled image`.
`Created`, then `Started`. `READY 1/1` means one of one containers is ready. `kubectl get` without `-n` looks in `default` and finds nothing.
`logs`, `exec` and `port-forward` all go through the API server. An edit inside the container is gone after you delete the Pod and apply the file again.

steps.note: `containerPort` is documentation. It does not open or block anything by itself. With a tag other than `latest`, the default pull policy is `IfNotPresent`: the node pulls the image once and reuses it. Deleting a Pod waits up to the default grace period, which the lesson says is 30 seconds.

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace `k8s-from-zero`. The lesson's cluster is named `k8s-ep04`, so node names on yours will differ. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What is a Pod, in the docs' words as the lesson quotes them?
exercises.a: A group of one or more containers with shared storage and network resources, and a specification for how to run the containers. You never ask Kubernetes to run a bare container.

exercises.q: Name the three properties the lesson says follow from that, and say where the IP lives.
exercises.a: One network identity: the IP belongs to the Pod, and containers in the same Pod talk on `localhost`. One hostname: containers see the Pod name. One place: all of the Pod's containers run on the same node.

exercises.q: Name the four required top-level fields, and the fifth field you see when you read an object back. Who writes the fifth?
exercises.a: `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata` and `spec`. The fifth is `status`, and the cluster writes it. You never put `status` in your file.

exercises.q: What does `containerPort` do, and what is the default pull policy for a tag other than `latest`?
exercises.a: `containerPort` is documentation. It tells readers and tools which port the process listens on. It does not open or block anything by itself. With a tag other than `latest`, the default pull policy is `IfNotPresent`: the node pulls the image once and reuses it.

exercises.q: Name the five Pod phases, and the three container states.
exercises.a: Phases: `Pending`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Unknown`. Container states: `Waiting`, `Running`, `Terminated`. The STATUS column is a friendly mix of both, and the lifecycle docs warn you not to confuse it with the phase.

exercises.q: What are the three `restartPolicy` values, and how does the restart wait grow?
exercises.a: `Always` (the default), `OnFailure`, or `Never`. The kubelet waits 10 seconds, then 20, then 40, doubling up to a cap of 5 minutes, and resets the timer once a container has run for 10 minutes without trouble.

exercises.q: Apply `pod.yaml` and run `kubectl get pods -n k8s-from-zero` at once, then again a few seconds later. What STATUS values does the lesson show, and what does `READY 1/1` mean?
exercises.a: First `ContainerCreating` with `READY 0/1`, then `Running` with `READY 1/1`. `1/1` means one of one containers is ready. Without `-n`, kubectl looks in `default` and finds nothing.

exercises.q: Read `kubectl describe pod hello -n k8s-from-zero` from the events upward. Which four reasons does the lesson list, in order?
exercises.a: `Scheduled` (the scheduler picked a node), then `Pulled`, `Created` and `Started` from the kubelet. On the lab the pull event says the image was already present. On your machine you see `Pulling` and then `Successfully pulled image`.

exercises.q: Run the three `kubectl exec` commands from step 6. What three facts do they confirm?
exercises.a: `nginx -v` prints the nginx version (the lesson shows nginx/1.29.8). `cat /etc/hostname` prints `hello`, the Pod name. `wget` of `http://localhost:80` returns the nginx welcome page. This image is Alpine-based, so it has `sh` and no `bash`.

exercises.q: Forward `8080:80` and curl the local port. What does the first terminal print when the curl arrives, and how do you stop the tunnel?
exercises.a: The first terminal prints `Handling connection for 8080`. The curl output includes `<title>Welcome to nginx!</title>`. Press Ctrl+C in the first terminal. Port-forward is a debugging tool for you alone.

exercises.q: Run the `grep -E` command from step 8, and the jsonpath that prints `.status.phase`. What five keys come back, and what is the phase?
exercises.a: The keys are `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec` and `status`. The phase is `Running`.

exercises.q: Apply `once.yaml`, `crash.yaml` and `typo.yaml`. After about a minute, what STATUS does each show in the lesson, and what phase is underneath `once`, `crash` and `typo`?
exercises.a: `once` is `Completed` and its phase is `Succeeded`. `crash` is `Error` (or `CrashLoopBackOff` while the kubelet waits) and its phase stays `Running`. `typo` is `ImagePullBackOff` and its phase is `Pending`, waiting reason `ImagePullBackOff`.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl logs crash -n k8s-from-zero --previous`. What two lines does the lesson show?
exercises.a: `starting` and `cannot find config`. `--previous` reads the log of the run that crashed, once the container has been restarted.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You write a heading into the container's `index.html`, delete the Pod, and apply `pod.yaml` again. What does a fetch of the page show, and why?
exercises.a: The original nginx title. The new Pod has the same name and a fresh container from the image, so the edit is gone. Anything you want to keep belongs in the image, in configuration, or on a volume.

exercises.q: Apply a Pod whose namespace is spelled `k8s-form-zero`. What error does the lesson quote?
exercises.a: `Error from server (NotFound): error when creating "pod.yaml": namespaces "k8s-form-zero" not found`. The cluster will not create a namespace for you. Fix the spelling, or create it with `kubectl create namespace`.

exercises.q: The manifest says `spec.contianers`. What does kubectl do, and which command looks up the real field name?
exercises.a: It rejects the file: `strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.contianers"`. kubectl validates strictly by default. Check spelling with `kubectl explain pod.spec.containers`.

exercises.q: `kubectl exec` of `bash` prints `exec: "bash": executable file not found in $PATH`. What does the lesson tell you to try?
exercises.a: Small images ship `sh` or nothing. Try `sh`. For an interactive shell the lesson uses `kubectl exec -it hello -n k8s-from-zero -- sh`.
